faq.a10: What kids do on a screen matters as much as how long. Short games that practise a skill, and making something of their own, are a good kind. Set your own limits with your device’s tools. Read our screen-time guide.

screen.lead: There’s no perfect number of minutes. What kids do on a screen, who they do it with and what it pushes them towards matter just as much. This checklist helps you judge any game or app, including ours.

check.li6: Making or scrolling: does your child solve, practise or make something, or mostly watch?

faq.a1: There is no single number. Paediatricians suggest consistent limits that leave room for sleep, school, being active and family time, and paying attention to what kids do on screens. A family media plan helps you decide.
faq.a2: Games can be educational. Look for ones where your child solves, practises or makes something, with no ads or purchases pulling them along.
